title: Chain-length-selective cooperative assembly underlies β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1
abstract: Abstract Lectin receptors recognize specific glycan features within heterogeneous glycan populations to initiate immune signaling, yet how defined signals are extracted from structurally diverse ligand mixtures remains poorly understood. Here we report the molecular basis by which the innate immune receptor Dectin-1 recognizes the soluble β-glucan laminarin. Native mass spectrometry revealed that laminarin exists as heterogeneous chains spanning a degree of polymerization (DP) of 22–44, while Dectin-1 is strictly monomeric in solution. Isotopic mass tagging with uniformly ¹³C-labeled Dectin-1 established a preferred 3:3 receptor-to-laminarin stoichiometry (~80–85 kDa). Flow-induced dispersion analysis demonstrated cooperative binding with an apparent dissociation constant of 46 μM and a Hill coefficient of ~3, accompanied by a large increase in hydrodynamic radius. Analysis of the bound ligand fraction revealed selective enrichment of chains with DP 25–36, defining a preferred chain-length window. High-speed atomic force microscopy showed that individual Dectin-1 molecules undergo cooperative clustering on both laminarin and the longer β-glucan scleroglucan, while chemical crosslinking provided independent evidence for ligand-induced receptor association. Together, these findings demonstrate that β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1 is governed by chain-length selectivity and cooperative receptor assembly, consistent with a molecular ruler mechanism in which lectin receptors extract specific biological information from heterogeneous glycan populations.

title: End-to-end mapping of membrane transport from chemical structure to microorganisms
abstract: Abstract Membrane transport is a fundamental biological process with profound implications for pharmacology, biotechnology, and microbiology. While computational approaches have largely adopted a protein-centric perspective to annotate transportomes, inferring transport function directly from the intrinsic properties of substrates remains a major challenge. Addressing transport at the compound level enables the systematic evaluation of whether molecules undergo active transport and by which mechanisms, independent of prior transporter annotation. Here, we introduce ChemProFlow, a comprehensive computational framework that redefines transport analysis from a substrate-centric perspective. By integrating geometric deep learning with orthology-based genomic mapping, ChemProFlow predicts molecular transportability, assigns transport mechanisms according to the Transporter Classification Database, and identifies the microorganisms encoding the corresponding transport systems. We show that this integrated pipeline enables scalable, end-to-end mapping of substrate-transporter-organism relationships, with broad applications in pharmacology for anticipating drug transport, in biotechnology for guiding strain engineering, and in microbiology for dissecting substrate utilization across diverse taxa. By capturing the chemical determinants of transportability, ChemProFlow generalizes to previously unseen substrates and provides a high-throughput framework for systematic exploration of molecular transport across diverse biological contexts.

Critical dynamics govern the evolution of political regimes
abstract: Abstract Political regimes lack a stable endpoint: they shift between more and less democratic configurations over time, as illustrated by historical democratic waves and recent backsliding. We analyse the historical trajectories of countries within a two-dimensional regime space derived from the principal components of the Varieties of Democracy dataset. We observe dynamics consistent with weak non-ergodicity, unfolding in an effective landscape of sparse and shifting basins of stability. Step sizes and sojourn times follow heavy-tailed distributions near the critical regime where mean values diverge, pointing to intermittent and heterogeneous regime change. A continuous time random walk model reproduces the average dynamics and trajectory-to-trajectory variability of the last three decades. The temporal evolution of the ergodicity breaking parameter recovers waves of democratisation and periods of heightened global political divergence, demonstrating the framework’s diagnostic potential. These results suggest that political regime evolution follows universal stochastic principles while remaining punctuated by unique historical pathways.

title: Direct observation of phase-space dynamics during energetic-particle-driven MHD bursts
abstract: Abstract The phase space (velocity and real space) dynamics of bulk ions is a critical issue for the heating scenario in magnetically confined plasma. Bulk ions accelerate parallel to the magnetic field, and the velocity distribution function can depart from a Maxwellian due to wave-particle interactions such as Landau and transit-time damping. Here we show flattening in velocity space (a decrease in the velocity gradient) and a rapid increase in ion energy parallel to the magnetic field within 0.1 ms of the onset of the MHD burst, by 30% at the location of the MHD burst in the Large Helical Device. In velocity space, the anisotropy of ion-velocity distribution due to the acceleration of ions parallel to the magnetic field disappears within the ion-ion collision time scale (2 ~ 3 ms). The transient increase in ion energy decays within 6 ms at the plasma periphery but persists much longer in the plasma core, contributing to the rise in core-ion energy.

Crystallinity control of spin torque efficiency in CuNi alloys
abstract: Abstract Light metals are gaining increasing attention in spintronics due to their advantageous properties over traditional heavy metals. This work investigates the origin of large spin torque efficiency ( ξ SOT ) in CuNi alloys using spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance in FeNi/CuNi bilayers. Polycrystalline CuNi shows a ξ SOT comparable to heavy metal Pt. By controlling crystallinity, we observe a significant modulation of ξ SOT , as epitaxial CuNi (001) and (111) films exhibit similar but markedly lower values than their polycrystalline counterparts. This suggests that the charge-spin conversion in CuNi is strongly influenced by crystallinity and primarily dominated by extrinsic scattering. Temperature-dependent studies further support a dominant contribution from extrinsic scattering in both paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases, with minimal contribution from spin fluctuations across the Curie temperature. Our findings deepen the understanding of charge-spin interconversion in light metals and highlight their potential for spintronic applications.

A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. Results Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1% increase in mAP and approximately a 5.6 times improvement in FPS compared to the original YOLOv5s. Conclusions These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight model and acceleration strategies effectively balance high accuracy with high-throughput onboard image processing. The developed UAV-edge computing system provides a promising prototype for future efficient nectar flowering status monitoring, with potential applications in smart apiculture.

MonkeyOCR: document parsing with a structure-recognition-relation triplet paradigm
abstract: Abstract We introduceMonkeyOCR, a document parsing model that advances the state of the art by leveraging a structure-recognition-relation (SRR) triplet paradigm. This design simplifies what would otherwise be a complex multi-tool pipeline and avoids the inefficiencies of processing full pages with giant end-to-end models. In SRR, document parsing is abstracted into three fundamental questions—“Where is it?” (structure), “What is it?” (recognition), and “How is it organized?” (relation)—corresponding to structure detection, content recognition, and relation prediction. To support this paradigm, we present MonkeyDoc, a comprehensive dataset with 4.5 million bilingual instances spanning over ten document types, which addresses the limitations of existing datasets that often focus on a single task, language, or document type. Leveraging the SRR paradigm and MonkeyDoc, we trained a 3B-parameter document foundation model. We further identify parameter redundancy in this model and propose contiguous parameter degradation (CPD), enabling the construction of models from 0.6B to 1.2B parameters that run faster with an acceptable performance drop. MonkeyOCR achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing previous open-source and closed-source methods, including Gemini 2.5 Pro. Additionally, the model can be efficiently deployed for inference on a single RTX 3090 GPU. Code and models will be released at https://github.com/Yuliang-Liu/MonkeyOCR .

BondNet: molecular bond perception from 3D coordinates with explicit hydrogen context
abstract: Abstract Inferring molecular bonds from atomic coordinates is necessary when a reliable molecular graph is unavailable. We study the contribution of explicit hydrogens to this task using BondNet, a PaiNN-based network that jointly predicts connectivity and heavy–heavy bond types. On 27,240 GEOM-DRUGS test records, exact heavy–heavy graph recovery is 99.83% for clean coordinates and 69.56% at Gaussian coordinate noise $$\sigma =0.20$$ σ = 0.20 Å. The corresponding rates on a separately selected cohort of 10,000 PubChem3D molecules are 98.43% and 64.60%. At the higher noise level, default RDKit recovers 3.64% of PubChem3D graphs exactly; a Hückel configuration examined after the initial evaluation recovers 46.73%. A heavy-only BondNet reaches 50.70% exact match on GEOM at $$\sigma =0.20$$ σ = 0.20 , and the explicit-H advantage persists under matched heavy-atom perturbations. An oracle model supplied with reference hydrogen counts reaches 82.03%, suggesting that hydrogen-derived valence information contributes substantially to the observed benefit. Removing H atoms from the explicit-H model at inference sharply reduces bond-type accuracy. These results highlight the difference between bond-level and complete-graph accuracy. The GEOM test set was inspected during development, and the findings do not extend to charged molecules or authentic generated geometries. Scientific contribution We compare explicit-H and heavy-only input under the same training schedule and use an oracle hydrogen-count control to probe the information H atoms contribute. Heavy–heavy graph metrics, a separate PubChem3D cohort, and chemically normalized baselines show where learned bond perception succeeds and where high bond-level accuracy obscures reconstruction failures.

Translation uniformity and evolutionary conservation are associated with microprotein mass spectrometry detectability
abstract: Abstract Background Non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs) encode many microproteins that are rarely detected by mass spectrometry (MS), hindering their annotation as proteins. The properties that make them detectable in public MS repositories are poorly understood. Results We analysed 7097 Ribo-seq-supported human ncORFs, 1725 of which have peptide evidence in PeptideAtlas builds, using 18 biological features and embeddings from the ESM2 protein language model (PLM) in logistic regression and ensemble classifiers (ROC-AUC 0.768 ± 0.006 over five runs). Translation uniformity across the ORF (Cumulative In-Frame Ribosome Footprint Uniformity, CIF_HBP), mammalian conservation of ORF structure (ORBLv_mammal) and predicted HLA class I-binding peptide density were top-ranked by both SHAP and permutation importance. Adding ESM2 embeddings to the three top biological features did not change ROC-AUC (0.689 in both cases; ΔAUC = 0.000 ± 0.003), possibly because ESM2 was pre-trained on much longer canonical proteins. About 90% of positives are supported by HLA immunopeptidomics alone and 99% by HLA data alone or together with non-HLA data, so the model largely reflects immunopeptidome visibility; because all ncORFs have Ribo-seq support, it predicts MS detectability conditional on translation; when whole biotypes were held out, AUC fell from 0.706 to 0.659–0.669. Of the 200 top-ranked ncORFs, 27 were identified in a Ribo-seq-guided proteogenomic study (5.26-fold over chance, p = 7.2 × 10⁻ 13 ) and 28 in a second, more recent dataset (6.9-fold over chance, p = 1.9 × 10⁻ 16 ; significant after Bonferroni or Holm correction for two tests). Conclusions Sustained translation across the ORF and evolutionary conservation of ORF structure are statistically associated with the cumulative MS detection of ncORF microproteins, but label-source bias, the absence of protein abundance as a feature and biotype-specific patterns limit generality. These associations can help prioritise candidates for targeted proteomic discovery.

title: Quantifying structural variants in chromosomes using landmark-based disparity
abstract: Abstract Background Chromosomal architecture has played a key role in the evolution of biodiversity. Detecting structural variants (SVs) on chromosomes has informed the study of speciation, sex determination, adaptation, and some of the earliest divergences in the tree of life. Here we present a computationally non-intensive approach based on geometric morphometrics, that uses coordinate data from conserved, single-copy DNA sequences as landmarks to quantify structural disparities of focal chromosomes via primary or haploid genome assemblies across multiple species, individuals, or cell types. Results Based on two approaches, we show that this ‘geno-metric’ method can be applied at micro- and macroevolutionary scales to discover and diagnose SVs. Using human X-linked single-copy genes and ultraconserved elements as genomic ‘landmarks’, we provide empirical demonstrations with amniote sex chromosomes, the Drosophila virilis group, and placental mammal genomes. Landmark-based structural disparity analysis effectively identifies chromosomal SVs and has parallels with traditional morphometrics regarding chromosome size, landmark orientation and landmark availability. Using simulations, we show that structural disparity inferred from ultraconserved elements is correlated with overall levels of chromosome evolution; an attribute which is consistent with observed disparity between and within mammalian orders. We found that the disparity patterns of SVs have significant phylogenetic signal, giving them broad importance for studying evolutionary biology. We also discuss alternative approaches that may be used to extract genomic coordinates and SV data for multi-species comparisons. Conclusions Structural disparity analysis is a reference free, whole-genome alignment free, non-pairwise comparative method that uses coordinates of single-copy genomic markers and dimensionality reduction methods to measure SVs on homologous chromosome sets. The method offers an intuitive, rapid mechanism to detect and measure SVs and consequently, offers the potential to reveal broader patterns of chromosome evolution related to expansions, contractions, rearrangements and phylogenetic history.

Aerobic preference in the marine protist Paradiplonema papillatum having anaerobic genomic potential
abstract: Abstract Background The diplonemid Paradiplonema papillatum is a marine planktonic protist with predicted complex and versatile metabolism. Investigation of carbohydrate metabolism and capacity for anaerobic life strategy revealed a disparity between its genomic and actual physiological preference. Despite possessing the genetic toolkit that should allow it to thrive in anoxic environment, P. papillatum primarily relies on aerobic metabolism, which it finely tunes in response to nutrient availability. Results Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) of the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle serves as a key regulatory switch. The NAD + - and NADP + -dependent IDH paralogues maintain the cycle’s plasticity, as this enzyme can support both the standard oxidative TCA cycle and its reductive branch, depending on metabolic requirements. The TCA cycle provides reduced cofactors, which branches into both canonical and non-canonical pathways when nutrients are abundant. This branched respiration is supported by ubiquinones UQ 8 and UQ 9 , whose biosynthetic pathway is a mosaic of a genes of different evolutionary origins. In addition to oxidative phosphorylation, P. papillatum can synthesize ATP in the propionate cycle and the acetate:succinate coenzyme A (CoA) transferase/succinyl-CoA synthetase cycle via substrate-level phosphorylation. Conclusions Our results highlight the complex regulation of mitochondrial metabolism in the diverse and abundant diplonemids and provide insight into the physiological strategies of marine planktonic microeukaryotes.

abstract: Abstract Flexible wearable sensors have transformed motion tracking, soft robotics, and human-machine interfaces by enabling precise movement detection and adaptability to curved surfaces. However, conventional composite sensors often face challenges such as limited sensitivity, detection range, linearity, and durability. In this study, we propose a stretchable auxetic sensing textile with a negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) structure, incorporating reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and carbon nanotubes (CNT) by micro-crack engineering to enhance its mechanical durability and sensing performance. Integrating macro-scale NPR with micro-scale wrinkles, this innovative design achieves a high sensitivity of 11.2 within a wide detection range (0–100%), a more linear sensing range with an R 2 value of 0.998, an ultra-low detection limit of 0.5%, and exceptional durability, outperforming conventional wearable sensors. Additionally, the textile sensor boasts excellent moisture permeability (32.7 g m −2 h −1 ) and a remarkable NPR value of −0.25, ensuring comfort and adaptability for various wearable applications. Integrated with deep learning algorithms, the auxetic sensing textile demonstrates 98% accuracy in recognizing soft robotic movements at various bending angles. It is capable of capturing both smallscale physiological signals, such as electrocardiograms, and large-scale movements, offering significant freedom of movement and adaptability to complex surfaces.

Long-term fatigue dimensions in the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI) up to five years after radiotherapy and their trajectories in men diagnosed with non-metastatic prostate cancer in the international REQUITE study
abstract: Abstract Background Fatigue is a common, multidimensional symptom in cancer patients. Little is known about fatigue dimensions and their trajectories in prostate cancer (PCa). Methods Using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI), 1097 men treated with radiotherapy for non-metastatic PCa (2014–2016) prospectively reported fatigue up to five years later. Prevalent fatigue was defined as scores ≥75th percentile in men aged ≥60 years in a German general population sample. Pre-radiotherapy patient characteristics were examined for their associations with general fatigue, physical fatigue, mental fatigue, reduced activity, and reduced motivation two years later using logistic regression models. Fatigue trajectories up to two years post-radiotherapy were explored using latent class growth analysis and multinomial regression. Results About 72% (785/1097) of patients reported being fatigued for at least one dimension in the MFI from before the start of radiotherapy up to five years later, with 45% (367/816) being fatigued two years post-radiotherapy. Pre-radiotherapy fatigue level (OR: 4.7–9.0), depression (OR: 2.5), diabetes (OR: 1.8–2.2), hypertension (OR: 1.6–1.8), and BMI (OR: 1.8–2.2) were statistically significant predictors of long-term fatigue two years post-radiotherapy across dimensions. Depression, BMI, and pelvic radiotherapy were associated with experiencing a high fatigue trajectory. Conclusions Early fatigue assessments, in addition to self-reported comorbidities and BMI, showed additional benefits beyond symptom detection by providing prognostic value for poorer long-term fatigue outcomes. Multidimensional fatigue assessments could guide tailored symptom management strategies, targeting specific dimensions to address associated impairments in quality of life and functioning.

High-accuracy graphene quantum Hall array resistance standards based on wye-delta transformation
abstract: Abstract The wye-delta (Y-∆) transformation has been demonstrated to significantly reduce the number of Hall bars necessary for high-resistance quantum Hall array resistance standards (QHARS), addressing the spatial limitation in the practical applications. Network designs have been described for graphene-based Y-∆ arrays to realize resistance values of $$77\frac{h}{2{e}^{2}}$$ 77 h 2 e 2 ( ≈ 1 MΩ), $$775\frac{h}{2{e}^{2}}$$ 775 h 2 e 2 ( ≈ 10 MΩ), and $$7748\frac{h}{2{e}^{2}}$$ 7748 h 2 e 2 ( ≈ 100 MΩ). A programmable QHARS is conceived based on a Y-network with multiple arms. We will present the magnetoresistance transport properties of Y-∆ array devices, followed by the precision measurements of three identical devices, each consisting of 28 Hall bars. At 1.6 K, two devices are quantized at $$77\frac{h}{2{e}^{2}}$$ 77 h 2 e 2 ( ≈ 1 MΩ) to within 80 nΩ/Ω at magnetic field as low as 5 T and 6 T, respectively. Such high accuracy is achieved without cryogenic current comparator, but through a solution that utelizes the triple-connections to the three terminals of the Y-∆ array device, a dual-source bridge (DSB), and a substitution method. Our results establish the viability of a LHe-free quantum Hall resistance (QHR) system with accuracy of a few parts in 10 8 for high-resistance calibration. This system is readily adoptable to improve traceability and reduce the calibration chain for industrial applications.

title: Contact-localized, strain-engineered metal contacts in 2D field-effect transistors: enabling low-barrier injection via a local stressor
abstract: Abstract Strain engineering has been an effective strategy for enhancing carrier transport in Si-based transistors. However, in atomically thin 2D materials, strain transfer is hindered by a weak van der Waals (vdW) interface, and global or substrate-mediated strain is difficult to apply effectively. Thus, strain engineering produces limited effects on performance improvement. To overcome these challenges, we report a contact-localized strain engineering approach using metal stressors for MoS 2 transistors. Effective strain is induced when three key mechanical conditions are satisfied: (1) metal nanoisland formation at the interface between metal and MoS 2 enabled by intermediate adhesion, moderate surface tension, and high adatom diffusivity on MoS 2 ; (2) strain generation arising from lattice and atomic registry interactions between the metal and MoS 2 at the interface; and (3) strain transfer through a finite vdW gap that suppresses hybridization while allowing shear coupling. The tensile strain in MoS 2 is exclusively confined to the footprint of the metal nanoisland and integrates to an average global strain of ~0.2%, while the interface remains non-reactive. This engineered strain lowers the effective Schottky barrier height by ~50 meV and reduces contact resistance by ~30%, thereby increasing the on-current by ~60% compared with otherwise identical unstrained devices. This work positions contact-localized strain control as a promising design knob for preparing high-performance 2D transistors.

title: Hypermethylation in CpG-rich cfDNA fragments enables accurate detection of circulating tumor DNA in BRCA1- and BRCA2-associated breast and ovarian cancer
abstract: Abstract Pathogenic BRCA 1 and BRCA2 germline variants confer an increased risk of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC). In this high-risk cohort, novel biomarkers are needed to support patient management. While circulating cell-free DNA-based conventional CpG-level averaging is promising, it dilutes tumor-specific signals in samples with low circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) fractions. Here, we developed a targeted ultra-deep NGS assay for detecting tumor-derived ctDNA based on fragment-level hypermethylation of CpG-rich cfDNA. A panel of 360 cancer-specific CpG-rich regions derived from 450k methylation array datasets from TCGA breast cancer and GEO ovarian cancer, was applied to plasma from 31 breast cancer, 16 ovarian cancer patients, and 26 healthy controls using enzymatic methylation sequencing. Hypermethylated ctDNA (hm-ctDNA) fragments, were significantly enriched in cancer cases, identifying 62.5% of ovarian and 38.7% of breast cancers at 100% specificity. Elevated hm-ctDNA was observed across different tumor stages, with higher burden in BRCA 1 -associated cases. This approach enables highly specific, non-invasive hypermethylated ctDNA detection in HBOC populations.

title: Coordinated patterns of genomic instability and immunogenicity predict 10-year breast cancer progression across subtypes and patient characteristics
abstract: Abstract Genomic instability is associated with breast cancer immune response. We sought to evaluate joint effects of genomic instability and immune response on recurrence using validated RNA-based assays and statistical models for assessing joint expression in a population-based dataset ( N = 2783). Prognostic value of the resulting coordinated signature, Repair, Immune, and Genomics for Oncologic Reclassification (RIGOR150), was assessed in estrogen receptor (ER)+ and ER− breast cancers ( N = 1899 with recurrence information) and validated in public datasets. RIGOR150 was strongly associated with recurrence risk in training (Hazard Ratio [HR] for high vs. low-risk = 5.10, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.19, 8.15) and test data (HR = 3.07, 95% CI = 1.73, 5.45) and was validated in external datasets. Among ER+ tumors, RIGOR150 high-risk was associated with early (0–5 years, HR = 5.75, 95% CI = 3.38, 9.77) and late recurrence (5–10 years, HR = 2.67, 95% CI = 1.26, 5.65). RIGOR150 added prognostic value independent of existing risk predictors (21-gene recurrence score and PAM50), and was associated with neoantigens, proliferation, and tumor-immune cell proximity. Overall, joint patterns of genomic instability and immunogenicity augment current breast cancer prognostic scores, providing early and late prognostication.

Role of defect trapping in the enhanced corrosion resistance of Ni–Mo alloys with yttrium and yttrium oxide additions
abstract: Abstract Corrosion of structural alloys remains a critical challenge for advanced molten salt reactors, where aggressive fluoride salts promote continuous dissolution at the salt–metal interface. While most mitigation strategies emphasize thermodynamic stability, kinetic control of atomic transport has received comparatively less attention. Here, we propose a corrosion mitigation strategy based on diffusion control and vacancy trapping by dilute yttrium (Y) solutes and yttrium oxide (Y 2 O 3 ) dispersions in Ni alloys. A combined computational and experimental approach integrates density functional theory (DFT), self-consistent mean-field (SCMF) diffusion modeling, and an impurity trapping model to quantify the impact of defect trapping on effective vacancy mobility. Strong first-nearest-neighbor vacancy–Y binding, off-lattice vacancy configurations, and elevated rotational and dissociation barriers result in pronounced suppression of vacancy diffusivity, while Y 2 O 3 -associated sites treated as fixed traps in the model further reduce the mobile vacancy population. Ni–Mo (NM), Y-modified (NMY), and Y 2 O 3 -containing (NMYO) alloys were tested in molten fluoride salt at 750 ∘ C. Corrosion penetration decreases systematically from NM to NMY to NMYO, consistent with the predicted reduction in vacancy-mediated transport. The same trend is observed in mass change, with net weight loss decreasing from 0.52% for NM to 0.23% for NMY and 0.09% for NMYO. These results are consistent with an alloy-side transport contribution from defect trapping and reduced atomic transport. This study therefore suggests point defect engineering as a promising alloy design strategy for extreme nuclear environments.

title: Direct observation of surface chemistry evolution for Ti-6Al-4V powders in calciothermic reduction recycling process
abstract: Abstract Titanium alloy powders are susceptible to oxygen pickup during handling, storage, and usage in additive manufacturing (AM), which degrades the 3D-printed parts’ mechanical properties and severely limits their reuse. Industrial AM titanium alloy feedstocks are subjected to stringent oxygen requirements, leading to large volumes of high-oxygen powder waste, which increases carbon footprint and cost. Thermochemical reduction with strong oxygen-affinity metals offers a viable route for titanium powder recovery, yet the oxygen removal mechanism from powder surfaces remains to be confirmed by direct experimental observation. Here, calciothermic reduction of AM-grade spherical Ti-6Al-4V powder is performed, followed by acid pickling and drying. Multiscale characterization is employed to correlate changes in bulk oxygen content, surface morphology, oxide-layer structure, and near-surface chemistry at the individual-particle level. Atom probe tomography reveals a graded oxygen profile extending from a TiO₂ outer surface through progressively oxygen-depleted subsurface regions into the α-Ti64 matrix. The oxidized and rejuvenated powders exhibit oxide regions of approximately 10 and <5 nm, respectively, while the matrix oxygen concentration decreased from about 3.2 to 0.5 at.%. A Ca–O-rich reaction-product layer and a narrow Ca–Ti–O interfacial region were directly observed after reduction, indicating that oxygen transfer occurs through a surface-mediated interfacial reaction.

title: Towards spatio-temporal extrapolation of phase-field simulations with convolution-only neural networks
Predicting Intergranular Corrosion Penetration Depth in Accelerated Testing using Machine Learning
Elucidating cesium solidification and stabilization mechanisms in nano-gamma-alumina modified cementitious matrices under realistic conditions
abstract: Abstract Ordinary Portland cement (OPC) matrices are widely used in low and intermediate level radioactive waste immobilization; however, improvements in waste loading, workability, durability, and radionuclide retention remain desirable. This work investigates the influence of nano-γ-Al₂O₃ modification on the short-and long-term solidification and stabilization performance of OPC-based cesium-bearing waste forms under ideal and realistic curing conditions. The synthesized nano-γ-Al₂O₃ particles exhibited mesoporous morphology, reactive hydroxylated surfaces, and negative surface charge suitable for cementitious applications. Under ideal curing conditions, nano-γ-Al₂O₃ displayed a non-monotonic dosage-dependent effect on the hydration and solidification behavior due to multi-variable interactions leading to changes in the nano- and matrix-chemical conditions thus affecting the pore-solution chemistry, and hydration pathways. 5 wt.% modified matrix provided improved workability, enhanced volumetric stability, and acceptable mechanical performance. Under realistic curing conditions and maximum waste loading, the 5 wt.% nano-γ-Al₂O₃ matrices maintained their favorable processing. Mineralogical, spectroscopic, and microstructural analyses revealed the formation of Al-rich hydration assemblages, including AFt, AFm, and hydroxo-AFm phases and the presence of more hydroxylated species in the modified matrix. Elemental-ratio distributions in pristine and leached matrices indicated that Cesium binding is primarily associated with C-S-H/C-A-S-H and AFt/AFm hydration products. The results demonstrate that while nano-γ-Al₂O₃ effectively tailors the workability and hydration pathways under representative waste-conditioning conditions, its implementation involves a performance trade-off between processing behavior, mechanical integrity, and long-term cesium retention.

title: Degradation-front evolution and micromechanical heterogeneity in cement pastes incorporating expansive agents under sodium sulfate attack
Impurity-driven corrosion and redox control of SS316H in molten NaCl–MgCl2 salts
Effect of plastic deformation on corrosion, biological and technological properties of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI implants
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical anodization improves the surface properties of titanium implants, but the resulting oxide layer may be damaged by plastic deformation during insertion or service. This study investigated how four deformation levels, together with an undeformed reference, affect anodized Ti6Al4V ELI. Surface morphology, roughness, wettability, microstructure, cytocompatibility, and electrochemical behavior were evaluated. Deformation progressively increased surface roughness and induced micro- and macrocracking of the anodic layer, while all surfaces remained hydrophilic. Damage to the oxide markedly reduced corrosion protection: the corrosion rate increased from approx. 50 to 650 nm year⁻¹, whereas polarization resistance decreased from 11,920 to 327 kΩ·cm². Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicated facilitated ionic transport through deformation-induced defects. Nevertheless, no cytotoxic effect on MC3T3-E1 cells was observed, and differences in cell viability were not statistically significant. Thus, plastic deformation substantially impairs the electrochemical barrier function of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI without adversely affecting its short-term cytocompatibility.

title: A state-of-the-art polygenic score for idiopathic Parkinson’s disease: benchmarking methods and impact on genetic PD carriers
abstract: Abstract Genetic causes are identified in up to 15% of Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients; the remaining idiopathic PD (iPD) patients are attributed to polygenic risk, environmental and lifestyle factors, and interactions thereof. We applied five advanced polygenic score (PGS) tools to data from 1762 iPD patients and 4227 healthy controls of European ancestry. 5-fold cross-validation revealed a significant boost in the discriminative power of modern Bayesian methods over simpler approaches, leading to the development of a novel iPD-PGS. This score demonstrated significantly improved performance compared to existing scores, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.680 (95% confidence interval (-CI):[0.665, 0.695]). External validation confirmed its robustness. Early-onset iPD patients exhibited higher PGS values than late-onset iPD patients and healthy controls, indicating increased polygenetic burden. Applying our novel iPD-PGS to carriers of heterozygous PRKN variants and GBA1 coding risk variants suggested that penetrance in these groups is partly explained by the same polygenic alterations as observed mitigating iPD. GBA1 showed a trend toward higher discriminative potential than PRKN ( GBA1 : AUC = 0.639, 95%-CI:[0.590, 0.687]; PRKN : AUC = 0.594, 95%-CI:[0.501, 0.687]), though confidence intervals overlapped. Our study highlights the potential of advanced PGSs in PD research, particularly in identifying high-risk individuals and modifying risk in rare-variant carriers.

title: Synergistic interplay between triazine and curcumin or resveratrol in mitigating rotenone-induced toxicity in Drosophila model
abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, oxidative stress, and debilitating motor dysfunction. Targeting the Wnt signaling pathway provides a powerful disease-modifying strategy. Building on recent evidence that triazine derivatives modulate Wnt signaling, we used a Drosophila model and in silico molecular docking to validate the specific interactions driving this pathway modulation, followed by qPCR of key Wnt signaling-related genes: armadillo , wingless , and frizzled 3 . The neuroprotective efficacy of the triazine derivative, alone or in combination with curcumin or resveratrol, was subsequently evaluated using behavioral, neurochemical, biochemical, apoptotic, immunohistochemical, and ultrastructural assessments. Treatment with the triazine derivative produced marked neuroprotective effects, which were further enhanced when combined with curcumin or resveratrol. This treatment significantly restored dopamine levels and locomotor performance, enhanced superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, and reduced lipid peroxidation compared with untreated rotenone-exposed flies. Moreover, immunohistochemical analysis indicated attenuation of apoptotic signaling, while transmission electron microscopy revealed substantial preservation of neural ultrastructure. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the neuroprotective potential of the triazine derivative and suggest that its combination with curcumin and resveratrol may provide an enhanced strategy for counteracting oxidative stress, neural apoptosis, and motor dysfunction associated with PD. The findings further support Wnt signaling modulation as a promising mechanistic target and provide a rationale for further investigations of triazine-based combination strategies as potential disease-modifying approaches for PD.

title: Longitudinal progression of digital arm swing measures during free-living gait in early Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Abstract Asymmetric arm swing reduction is a hallmark of early-stage Parkinson’s disease (PD). We evaluated wrist sensor-based arm swing measures during free-living gait as digital progression biomarkers in 623 early-stage PD participants and 50 controls monitored continuously for one year (controls) or two years (PD). Biweekly measures were extracted from detected gait segments without other arm activities using a previously validated signal processing pipeline. Arm swing measures were reduced in PD, reduced on the most affected side, moderately correlated with clinical motor severity, and highly reliable. In unmedicated participants, most affected side measures declined over one year (standardized response means: −0.34 to −0.85) and all but one over two years ( −0.57 to −1.06). The corresponding MDS-UPDRS Part III subscore showed SRMs of −0.26 (95% CI [−0.66, 0.06]) at one year and −0.85 (95% CI [-1.95, -0.24]) at two years. In medicated participants, arm swing increased on the most affected side, which was associated with higher dopaminergic doses and dyskinesia. Overall, free-living arm swing measures are promising progression biomarkers in early, untreated PD.

title: Plasma proteomic signatures of Parkinson’s disease status, cognitive heterogeneity and longitudinal decline
Computer vision-derived gait-state tracking of acute treatment response in Parkinson’s disease: external and prospective validation
abstract: Abstract Continuous, treatment-responsive measurement of motor state is an unmet need in Parkinson’s disease and a broad challenge for digital biomarkers: clinical gait scales are coarse and ordinal, and most digital measures are never validated beyond their derivation setting. We present a digital biomarker derived from full-mesh 3D human-pose reconstruction in standard monocular video, built from high-contrast within-patient treatment transitions and applied to out-of-sample patients. In a retrospective cohort (53 patients) it discriminated treatment states (cross-validated AUROC 0.88) and defined a continuous motor-state axis. Across six independent cohorts (266 subjects, 3,591 walks, eight sites, three continents) it showed consistent medication effects in the two medication-labelled cohorts and tracked clinical gait impairment in the four cohorts carrying clinical gait ratings; in a prospective cohort (21 patients) it preserved ordered transitions for medication and deep brain stimulation. On identical paired observations it was more responsive than the ordinal MDS-UPDRS Part III item 3.10 (standardized response mean 1.29 versus 0.83 internally, 0.92 versus 0.54 externally); its finer resolution also registered directional within-patient improvement more often, an advantage of measurement resolution that reaches parity once change is required to exceed the minimal detectable change, supporting a scalable, generalizable measurement tool.

title: Combined STN-DBS and acupuncture modulate cortico-striatal oscillations and CSF tracer distribution in anxious Parkinsonian rats
Association of multisystem vascular-related disease with incident parkinsonism: insights from a cohort study
abstract: Abstract Systemic vascular dysfunction has been implicated in parkinsonism, but prospective evidence on the cumulative burden of multisystem vascular-related disease (MVRD) and its relation to genetic susceptibility remains limited. We included 456,862 UK Biobank participants of White ethnicity with available genetic data who were free of diagnosed parkinsonism at baseline. MVRD comprised ischemic heart disease, stroke, chronic kidney disease, retinopathy, and neuropathy. Incident parkinsonism, excluding vascular parkinsonism, was ascertained during follow-up. Fine–Gray competing-risk models were used to estimate subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with all-cause mortality treated as the competing event. During a median follow-up of 11.8 years, 2559 incident parkinsonism cases occurred. Any MVRD was associated with a higher risk of parkinsonism (sHR 1.35; 95% CI 1.23, 1.48), and each additional MVRD-related condition was associated with a higher risk (sHR 1.30; 95% CI 1.21, 1.40). The associations increased with the number of MVRD-related conditions, with sHRs of 1.29, 1.73, and 2.52 for one, two, and three or more conditions, respectively, compared with none. The association between MVRD and parkinsonism was observed in both low- and high-genetic-risk groups, with no evidence of interaction. Results remained broadly consistent after excluding cases diagnosed during the first 10 years of follow-up. These findings suggest a graded association between MVRD burden and incident parkinsonism, adding to the evidence linking vascular health to neurodegeneration.
